verses.1: And now, Israel, hear these laws and rules that I have taught you. Follow them so that you may live and inherit the land that Jehovah, your God, has given you.
verses.2: Do not add anything to what I command you. Do not deviate from these commands, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you.
verses.3: Your eyes shall see what Jehovah has done to the man of Peor. For every man who followed in the footsteps of the man of Peor, Jehovah, your God, destroyed him from among you.
verses.4: And you will be united with your God. You will all live forever, today.
verses.5: See, I have given you laws and regulations, as Jehovah, my God, has commanded me to do. These laws must be obeyed while you are on this land, where you are about to inherit it.
verses.6: And you have kept and carried out these laws, because they are your wisdom and knowledge. In front of the nations who will hear all these laws, they will say, “This is indeed a wise and intelligent people.”
verses.7: For there is no great nation whose gods are closer to them than our God, who hears all our prayers.
verses.8: And who is there among the nations that has laws and righteous judgments, just as all this Torah I give you today does?
verses.9: Only keep these things for yourself, and protect your soul from forgetting what your eyes have seen. Let them remain in your heart throughout your life, so that you and your children can remember them.
verses.10: The day when you stand before Jehovah your God in the wilderness. Then Jehovah says to me, “Let the people listen to my words.” They must learn to fear me throughout all the days they live on this earth. And they must also teach their descendants to fear me.
verses.11: And they came forward and stood beneath the mountain. The mountain was covered with fire, until it darkened the sky. Clouds and rain covered everything.
verses.12: And the LORD spoke to you through the fire. It was a voice of words that you heard, but you did not see the light of His voice.
verses.13: And he will tell you about his covenant. He has commanded you to do ten things. These things are written on two stone tablets.
verses.14: And at that time, the LORD commanded me to teach you the laws and regulations that you must follow in the land you are about to enter.
verses.15: And you shall be preserved greatly for your souls, for you did not see any miracle on the day Jehovah spoke to you from within the fire.
verses.16: Do not create idols for yourselves; do not make any symbols or images, whether male or female.
verses.17: You shall make every bird that is on the earth; you shall make every wing that flies in the heavens.
verses.18: You build every creature on the earth; you create every fish that lives in the water, beneath the earth.
verses.19: And if your eyes should be opened, and you should see the sun, the stars, and all the heavenly beings. Then you will be disgraced, and you will worship them and serve them. For this is what Jehovah your God has given you as a gift to all nations under heaven.
verses.20: And Jehovah took you away from the iron chains of Egypt, so that you could become His people as it is today.
verses.21: And Jehovah was pleased with their words. So I did not cross the Jordan River, nor enter the good land that Jehovah your God has given you as a inheritance.
verses.22: For I am dead in this land. I cannot cross the Jordan River, but you can do so. You shall inherit this good land.
verses.23: Keep this covenant in your minds, so that you will not forget the covenant that Jehovah your God has made with you. You have made yourselves a reproach to all those who are called by Jehovah’s name.
verses.24: For Jehovah your God is an eating fire; he is a jealous God.
verses.25: For you will bear sons and grandsons, and they will inherit the land. But you have done evil in the eyes of Jehovah your God.
verses.26: I will testify to you today that the heavens and the earth are about to be destroyed. They will be destroyed soon from above the earth, as you cross the Jordan River. It will not be possible for them to last forever; they will surely be destroyed.
verses.27: And Jehovah will scatter you among the nations. You will be left out of the number of those who are counted among the nations, because Jehovah will govern you as He has planned.
verses.28: And serve there the God of man’s hands—a tree and a stone that neither see nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
verses.29: And ask Jehovah your God there for help. Then you will find that He will answer you with all your heart and soul.
verses.30: In your distress, and when you found yourself in all these situations, you returned to Jehovah, your God. You heard His voice.
verses.31: For the Lord, your God, is merciful. He will not abandon you or destroy you. He will not forget the covenant He made with your ancestors.
verses.32: For I ask you, in those ancient days before you came into existence, from the time when God created man on the earth, and from the edges of the heavens to the ends of them, whether this great thing will happen or not.
verses.33: Hear the voice of God speaking from within the fire. Just as you heard it, so shall you live.
verses.34: May God come and take away those nations from their positions near each other, through war, with weapons, and with great power. May He do this in all the ways that Jehovah your God has done for you in Egypt, before your eyes.
verses.35: Do you realize that Jehovah is the only God? He is not the same as any other god.
verses.36: From the heavens, you sent out your voice to warn us; and on the earth, you showed us the great fire. And what you said was heard through the flames.
verses.37: And because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants as his own. He brought you forth in his great power from Egypt.
verses.38: To destroy great nations and mighty armies from before you, so that you may take their land as a possession, just as it is today.
verses.39: And today, you shall know and understand in your heart that Jehovah is the God who exists above in heaven, and below on the earth. There is no other god besides Him.
verses.40: And you shall keep His laws and commandments, which I have commanded you today. May it be good for you and your children after you. And may it be a blessing to you, so that you may live on the land that the LORD your God gives you for all time.
verses.41: Then Moses will distinguish three cities across the Jordan River, from east to west.
verses.42: Let him be killed by someone who kills his neighbor without knowing it. And let him not suffer any harm or suffering from this act. Let him go to one of those cities and live there.
verses.43: Ets-Betser in the desert, in the land of Mishor L’Roubeni; and Ramat in Gilad for the Gadim; and Golan in Bashan for the Menashim.
verses.44: And this is the Torah that Moses placed before the children of Israel.
verses.45: These are the laws, commandments, and regulations that Moses commanded the children of Israel when they left Egypt.
verses.46: Across the Jordan, in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled over the region where Moses and the Israelites were struck by God when they left Egypt.
verses.47: And they inherited their land. These were two kings of the Amorites, who lived beyond the Jordan, to the east of the sun.
verses.48: From the edge of the valley along the banks of the Arnon River, all the way to Mount Shimon, that’s Hermon.
verses.49: And all the desert stretches from the east along the Jordan River, all the way to the sea in Arabia, under the rule of Ashdod.
